paragraphs.title: The Spirit Poured Out on All People

answers: Fire
His spirit
Water
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.”
easy.q: What will the Lord pour out upon all flesh?

answers: Upon all flesh
Only upon the old men
Only upon kings
easy.explanation: The promise is made to “all flesh,” meaning all kinds of people.
easy.q: Upon whom will the Lord pour out His spirit?

answers: Build temples
Prophesy
Escape from fire
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “your sons and your daughters shall prophesy.”
easy.q: What will the sons and daughters do?

answers: Old men shall dream dreams, and young men shall see visions
Only young men shall dream dreams
Old men and young men shall receive exactly the same description
medium.explanation: The passage says that old men shall dream dreams and young men shall see visions.
medium.q: What distinction between age groups is described in these verses?

answers: Upon all animals
Upon people without distinction of age, gender, or status
Only upon the children of Israel
medium.explanation: The promise includes people of different ages, genders, and social positions.
medium.q: What does “upon all flesh” mean in this passage?

answers: Servants and handmaids
Kings and priests
Soldiers and merchants
medium.explanation: The Lord says He will pour out His spirit “upon the servants and upon the handmaids.”
medium.q: Who is specifically included besides sons, daughters, old men, and young men?

answers: The spirit is only for people of high status
The promise includes people of low social status
Servants and handmaids are excluded from the promise
challenge.explanation: Their inclusion shows that the promise reaches people of every social status.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the mention of servants and handmaids?

answers: They all receive some expression of the Lord’s spirit
Only the old men receive the Lord’s spirit
Every group is forbidden to prophesy
challenge.explanation: The verses include different groups under the promise of the poured-out spirit.
challenge.q: What idea is shared by all the people described in these verses?

answers: Prophecy, dreams, and visions
Fire, blood, and smoke
Deliverance, a city, and a mountain
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions sons and daughters prophesying, old men dreaming dreams, and young men seeing visions.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly lists the spiritual gifts mentioned?

paragraphs.title: Signs and Wonders Before the Day of the Lord

answers: Blood, fire, and pillars of smoke
Water, wind, and lightning
Snow, clouds, and a rainbow
easy.explanation: The KJV says there will be “wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke.”
easy.q: What will appear in the heavens and on the earth before the day of the Lord?

answers: It will shine more brightly
It will be turned into darkness
It will become blood
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “The sun shall be turned into darkness.”
easy.q: What will happen to the sun?

answers: Blue
Black
Like blood
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “the moon into blood.”

answers: After the day of the Lord
Before the great and terrible day of the Lord
Only after the deliverance
medium.explanation: The signs are described as occurring before the great and terrible day of the Lord.

answers: In the sea and in the mountains
In the heavens and on the earth
In the city and in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The passage says there will be wonders “in the heavens and in the earth.”
medium.q: In which two realms will the wonders appear?

answers: Columns or rising masses of smoke
Drops of water falling from heaven
Rays of light from the moon
medium.explanation: The phrase describes upright columns or streams of smoke.
medium.q: What are “pillars of smoke” in this passage?

answers: First the day of the Lord, then the signs
First the signs, and then the day of the Lord
The signs and the day of the Lord are said to occur only after deliverance
challenge.explanation: The signs are presented as occurring before the coming of the day of the Lord.
challenge.q: What order is presented in these verses?

answers: The sun becomes dark and the moon appears as blood
The sun becomes red and the moon disappears
The sun and moon become white
challenge.explanation: The sun is turned into darkness, and the moon into blood.
challenge.q: What changes in the appearance of the heavenly bodies are described?

answers: They involve the earth, the heavens, and striking changes in light and appearance
They concern only the social status of people
They describe only the refuge found in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The passage combines signs on earth with changes involving the sun and moon.
challenge.q: Which statement best summarizes the signs in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Deliverance and Refuge in Mount Zion and Jerusalem

answers: Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord
Only old men
Only those who live in the mountains
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered.”

answers: Mount Zion and Jerusalem
The wilderness and the sea
Galilee and Samaria
easy.explanation: The passage says that in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be deliverance.
easy.q: Which places are mentioned as places of deliverance?

answers: Those whom the Lord shall call
Those who built the city
Those who saw the fire
easy.explanation: The KJV refers to “the remnant whom the Lord shall call.”
easy.q: Who are the remnant mentioned in the passage?

answers: Those who call on the Lord’s name shall be delivered
Those who call on the Lord’s name shall see smoke
Those who call on the Lord’s name shall dream a dream
medium.explanation: The verse directly connects calling on the Lord’s name with deliverance.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between calling on the Lord and the result?

answers: They are places of deliverance
They are places where smoke will appear
They are places where visions will be seen
medium.explanation: The passage says that deliverance shall be found in Mount Zion and Jerusalem.
medium.q: What is the role of Mount Zion and Jerusalem in the passage?

answers: Rescue or being saved
The appearance of the moon
A pillar of smoke
medium.explanation: Here, deliverance means rescue or salvation.
medium.q: What does “deliverance” mean in this context?

answers: Those who call on the Lord shall be delivered, and the remnant includes those whom the Lord calls
Only the remnant may call on the Lord
The remnant has no connection with deliverance
challenge.explanation: The passage presents both deliverance for those who call on the Lord and a remnant whom the Lord shall call.
challenge.q: What relationship between the general promise and the remnant appears in the passage?

answers: Both are mentioned as places where deliverance shall be found
Both are described as places of fire
Both are mentioned as places of dreams
challenge.explanation: Both places are named in connection with deliverance.
challenge.q: What do Mount Zion and Jerusalem have in common in this verse?

answers: Deliverance is connected with calling on the Lord’s name, and the remnant consists of those whom He calls
Deliverance depends on seeing the moon, and the remnant depends on dreams
Deliverance is only for young men, and the remnant is only for servants
challenge.explanation: This summary follows the two deliverance statements in the passage.
challenge.q: Which statement most accurately summarizes the condition of deliverance?
